text: Have you ever wondered how to make technology work
for you instead of spending hours figuring everything out
Welcome to episode 19 of AI for Beginners Today
we’re looking at ai for presentations By the end
you’ll understand one practical idea watch a realistic example
and try a small exercise yourself You don’t need
a technical background or expensive software Bring your curiosity
We’ll work through it together Here’s the example we’ll
use a six-slide presentation about recycling We’ll use that
situation to make the topic concrete Watch how we
break the task into small steps because the same
thinking will help you use many different AI tools
later in this course
Let’s start with the main idea outline a slide
deck around one key message Think of AI as
a tool that processes information and returns an output
based on its training instructions and any relevant information
it can access It can save time on drafts
and patterns but it doesn’t automatically know what’s correct
for your situation The most useful habit is to
define what you want before touching the tool Ask
yourself three questions what’s my goal what information does
the tool need and how will I check the
result Those questions work whether you’re writing a prompt
building a workflow or reviewing a generated answer
Let’s try it with an example Our example is
a six-slide presentation about recycling Start by writing down
the desired result in one sentence Next identify the
input what would a person need to know to
do this task correctly Then write a simple instruction
with that context and a clear format On screen
I am showing a sample request followed by a
possible output Notice that we’re not judging the result
by how impressive it sounds We’re checking whether it
actually meets the task If the output is too
broad ask for a more specific version If a
fact matters verify it from a reliable source Pause
the video here if you’d like to copy the
structure into your own notes
Your turn Try this exercise generate slide titles and
speaker notes Begin with a very small example not
a complex project Give yourself thirty seconds to decide
what success would look like Then complete the task
once and inspect the result What’s useful What’s missing
What would you change Make one improvement and compare
the first and second versions This simple before-and-after comparison
teaches you more than copying a complicated prompt from
Before we finish remember this important limitation verify facts
and use licensed visuals Responsible AI use means understanding
the strengths of the tool and keeping yourself accountable
for the final result Today you learned that outline
a slide deck around one key message saw the
example of a six-slide presentation about recycling and practiced
a small hands-on task Here’s your challenge repeat the
exercise with a different topic and write down one
thing
